claims.claim: HTTPX allows specifying timeout behavior in more fine grained detail.
claims.citation: HTTPX also allows you to specify the timeout behavior in more fine grained detail.

claims.claim: HTTPX has four different types of timeouts: connect, read, write, and pool timeouts.
claims.citation: There are four different types of timeouts that may occur. These are connect, read, write, and pool timeouts.

claims.claim: The HTTPX connect timeout specifies the maximum amount of time to wait until a socket connection to the requested host is established.
claims.citation: The connect timeout specifies the maximum amount of time to wait until a socket connection to the requested host is established.

claims.claim: HTTPX raises a `ConnectTimeout` exception if it is unable to connect within the connect timeout.
claims.citation: If HTTPX is unable to connect within this time frame, a `ConnectTimeout` exception is raised.

claims.claim: The HTTPX read timeout specifies the maximum duration to wait for a chunk of data to be received.
claims.citation: The read timeout specifies the maximum duration to wait for a chunk of data to be received

claims.claim: A chunk of the response body is an example of a chunk of data covered by the HTTPX read timeout.
claims.citation: for example, a chunk of the response body

claims.claim: HTTPX raises a `ReadTimeout` exception if it is unable to receive data within the read timeout.
claims.citation: If HTTPX is unable to receive data within this time frame, a `ReadTimeout` exception is raised.

claims.claim: The HTTPX write timeout specifies the maximum duration to wait for a chunk of data to be sent.
claims.citation: The write timeout specifies the maximum duration to wait for a chunk of data to be sent

claims.claim: A chunk of the request body is an example of a chunk of data covered by the HTTPX write timeout.
claims.citation: for example, a chunk of the request body

claims.claim: HTTPX raises a `WriteTimeout` exception if it is unable to send data within the write timeout.
claims.citation: If HTTPX is unable to send data within this time frame, a `WriteTimeout` exception is raised.

claims.claim: The HTTPX pool timeout specifies the maximum duration to wait for acquiring a connection from the connection pool.
claims.citation: The pool timeout specifies the maximum duration to wait for acquiring a connection from the connection pool.

claims.claim: HTTPX raises a `PoolTimeout` exception if it is unable to acquire a connection within the pool timeout.
claims.citation: If HTTPX is unable to acquire a connection within this time frame, a `PoolTimeout` exception is raised.

claims.claim: The maximum number of allowable connections in the HTTPX connection pool is configured by the `limits` argument.
claims.citation: the maximum number of allowable connections in the connection pool, which is configured by the `limits` argument

claims.claim: HTTPX allows configuring the timeout behavior for any of the connect, read, write, and pool timeout values.
claims.citation: You can configure the timeout behavior for any of these values
